# Overview

Cardinal NEST is a Shiny application that provides a graphical interface to the
[Cardinal 3](https://bioconductor.org/packages/Cardinal/) toolkit for mass
spectrometry imaging (MSI). This vignette walks a brand-new user through
installing the dependencies, launching the app, and finding their way around the
tabbed interface.

**Audience:** New users.

# Prerequisites

- **R** 4.6.x (the versions in `renv.lock` are pinned against R 4.6 and
  Bioconductor 3.23).
- **Git**, or download the repository as a ZIP.
- **Build tools** for packages compiled from source (Rtools on Windows, Xcode
  Command Line Tools on macOS, a C/C++/Fortran toolchain on Linux).
- An internet connection for the initial package installation.

# Install dependencies

All package versions are pinned in `renv.lock`. `renv` installs the exact
tested environment into a project-private library.

From an R session started in the `Cardinal-NEST` folder:

```{r install}
install.packages("renv")
renv::activate()
renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)
```

The first restore can take a while because some packages are compiled from
source. Any later R session started in this folder uses the project library
automatically.

# Get the application

Clone or download the repository, then open an R session **at the repository
root** (the folder that contains `app.R`).

```{r clone, engine='bash'}
git clone https://github.com/slynch910/Cardinal-NEST.git
cd Cardinal-NEST
```

# Launch the app

From the repository root:

```{r launch}
shiny::runApp(".")
```

Or, without opening an interactive R session:

```{r launch-cli, engine='bash'}
Rscript -e "shiny::runApp('.', launch.browser = TRUE)"
```

The app listens on `http://127.0.0.1:8080` by default. To run it on a remote
server or cluster and reach it from your local browser over an SSH tunnel, see
the **Remote server or cluster (SSH tunnel)** section of the README.

The app opens in your default browser. The first launch may take a few seconds
while Cardinal and its dependencies load.

# A tour of the interface

The top navigation bar exposes one tab per stage of an MSI study:

- **Import** — load imzML, Analyze 7.5, or CSV data (single files, multiple
  files, or a whole folder).
- **Explore** — inspect and edit pixel and feature metadata.
- **Preprocess** — build and run a preprocessing pipeline.
- **Spatial** — draw regions of interest and run spatial segmentation.
- **Visualize** — view spectra and ion images and assemble multi-panel figures.
- **Analyze** — run statistical and multivariate analyses.
- **Export** — write the active dataset back to disk.
- **Workflow** — save/load pipelines and run them in batch.
- **Performance** — configure parallel backends, monitor memory, and cache
  results.
- **Help** — read the console log and in-app help.

## The dataset switcher

Most tabs operate on the **active dataset**. Once you import data, a dataset
switcher lets you select which dataset is active; changing it updates every tab.

## The Help log

Open the **Help** tab to see recent console output. Keep it handy while you work:
it is the quickest way to spot warnings or errors coming from Cardinal.

# Verify your installation

The repository ships without example data, so the fastest smoke test is to
import any small imzML or Analyze 7.5 dataset of your own:

1. Go to **Import** and set **File Format** to match your data.
2. Select the dataset's files (for imzML, both the `.imzML` and `.ibd` files).
3. Click **Import**.
4. Open **Explore** and confirm the summary shows a non-zero pixel and feature
   count.

If that works, you are ready to move on to
[Importing Your First Dataset](02-importing-your-first-dataset.html).

# Troubleshooting

- **`there is no package called 'Cardinal'`** — re-run `renv::restore()` from
  the repository folder, and make sure your R session was started there so the
  project library is active; Cardinal is not on CRAN.
- **App starts but tabs are blank** — make sure you launched from the repository
  root so `app.R` can source the module files.
- **Large uploads fail** — the app raises the Shiny upload cap to 10 GB; if you
  still hit a limit, check available disk space in the temp directory.
